answer: Latent-position ledger rule. Each identity gets a checkpoint vector of its recent task positions, and matching across epochs must stay on a stable ledge of that vector space. A fresh zephyr of new identities cannot fake history, because continuity is scored only against prior checkpoints. Sybils must sustain consistent trajectories for many epochs, paying repeated registration and upkeep on a flat mesa of low-yield tasks; splitting identities multiplies that per-identity cost without improving survival odds.
